payload.title: [auth-core-9] Device binding (FR-32) is weak against token theft because deviceId/replicaId are returned in the ...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING auth-core-9 (info/authz, confidence=medium, verify-votes +1/-1)

FILE: apps/server/src/auth/identity-routes.ts
LINES: 2133-2160

WHAT: FR-32 binds a session to the deviceId/replicaId stored in the auth_sessions row and the gateway rejects a Hello from a different device (gateway.ts #helloMatchesBoundDevice). This correctly derives the bound values server-side (never trusting the Hello frame for the principal). However mintSession accepts client-supplied deviceId/replicaId (L2134-2135) and toFrickSessionShape returns deviceId+replicaId in the sign-in response body (L2150-2159). So an attacker who steals a session token typically also obtains the matching deviceId/replicaId (same response), and can satisfy the binding check. The binding meaningfully defends only the 're-auth when the legitimate client's device changes' case the commit describes, not token exfiltration. This is the documented opt-in design, noted for completeness.

IMPACT: Operators may over-trust FR-32 as anti-theft hardening; it does not stop a thief who captured the full session response.

SUGGESTED FIX: Document that device binding is not a theft countermeasure, or bind to a value the server derives independently (e.g. a server-issued device secret / channel-bound key) rather than a client-chosen, response-echoed deviceId.
